title: Two-Arm Landmine Press
summary: A two-handed landmine press with interlocked hands, working the upper chest and front delts at a steep incline.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: landmine attachment; barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for front delts (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.6 for chest (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.6 for triceps (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.2 for side delts: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly side delts total.

setup.text: Hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands cupped together.
Lean slightly into the bar and press it up and away until your arms are straight.
Lower it back to your chest under control.

form_cues.cue: Lower under control to the chest
Press from the chest, not the legs. Keep the knees soft but still.

mistakes.text: Arching back instead of leaning into the bar.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: One side at a time.
Swap sheet: More stable, Less systemic fatigue, Easier to learn.

notes: Ratings, swap attributes and cues are the library model (modeled). An authored page will replace this one.
